newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian 35-day T-bill tender draws poor interest.
newsitem.headline: Canadian 35-day T-bill tender draws poor interest.

text.p: Today's auction of C$3 billion in 35-day Government of Canada T-bills was poorly bid but the results should not hurt outcome of the weekly T-bill tender at 1315 EDT/1715 GMT, dealers said.
"Just going into it there was definately a lack of interest," said one T-bill dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "It was definately a little bit sloppy."
The auction, which produced an average yield of 3.193 percent had tail of 10 basis points and high-low spread of 19 basis points.
The Government of Canada one-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 3.22 percent in the wake of the auction, up from 2.95 percent at Monday's close.
The dealer said the high average yield of the issue helped to attract some account buying after the initial release of auction results.

Concern about U.S. non-farm payrolls data tomorrow, the conclusion of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee meeting this afternoon were the large amount of supply all contributed to the lack of interest in the 35-day T-bill auction, said Rob Palombi, senior fixed-income analyst with MMS International.
Palombi said the poor results of the cash management bill were unlikely to have a major impact on this afternoon's auction.
The Government of Canada this afternoon will auction C$4.7 billion in three-month, six-month and one-year T-bills.
